verdict.rationale: LiveKit documents a quickstart for building and deploying a voice assistant in under 10 minutes, a no-code browser Agent Builder, model and voice access through LiveKit Inference, and a telephony stack for inbound and outbound calls. The evidence never shows getting a phone number directly. It mentions trunks, which suggests an external SIP provider is needed, and the quick timeline is claimed only for the browser voice assistant, not for a live phone call. missing for 10: documented phone-number provisioning, an end-to-end phone quickstart showing a first live call within an hour, explicit voice selection, independent hands-on corroboration of the phone path

support.subject: As a developer, I can build a working phone voice agent — prompt, voice, and phone number — and take my first live call within an hour

citations.quote: Build and deploy a simple voice assistant with Python or Node.js in less than 10 minutes.
LiveKit Agent Builder: Prototype and deploy voice agents directly in your browser, without writing any code.
Works seamlessly with LiveKit's telephony stack, allowing your agent to make calls to or receive calls from phones.
LiveKit telephony lets you build AI-powered voice apps that handle inbound and outbound calls.
Outbound trunks are used to place outgoing calls.
